title: God hates it.
paragraphs:
God hates it.
And you’re still entertaining it.

Because this isn’t about them.
Not the corrupt.
Not the violent.
Not the obvious sinners.

You’ve heard “God is love.”
But you were never told…
what He hates.

And maybe that’s why some things in your life
still feel… untouched.

Because if you really saw it the way God sees it—
you wouldn’t flirt with it anymore.
Let me open the tension wider.

What if the very thing you’ve been justifying…
is on God’s hate list?

What if the quiet attitudes, the hidden patterns,
the “it’s not that bad” moments—
are the very things heaven calls abomination?

“There are six things that the Lord hates,
seven that are an abomination to Him…”
— Proverbs 6:16–19
The silent belief that you’re okay without surrender.

You still pray—
but you don’t bow.

You still sing—
but you don’t submit.

You still post—
but you don’t repent.
Pride doesn’t always look like rebellion.
Not just lies you tell others.

“It’s just this once.”
“I can stop anytime.”
“God understands.”
And He still calls it sin.

“Everyone who is angry with his brother will be liable to judgment…”
— Matthew 5:22

Hatred begins in the heart
long before it reaches the hands.

Character assassination.
Online tearing down.
Cancel culture disguised as righteousness.

You didn’t spill blood—
but you crushed a soul.

You knew it was wrong—
but you still prepared for it.
“Feet that are swift to run to evil…”

When temptation shows up—
you don’t resist.

Something inside you
is being trained…
“A false witness who breathes out lies…”
Narratives shaped to protect your image.

And God says:
I see the whole thing.
“And one who sows discord among brothers.”

Gossip.
Division.
Subtle seeds of offense.
This is where shame creeps in.

“See? This is who you are.”
“You’re too far gone.”
“You can’t change.”
But that voice is lying too.
Because Scripture doesn’t stop at exposure.
God doesn’t reveal sin to destroy you.
He reveals it to save you.

Because the same Bible that says God hates sin
also says this:

“But God shows His love for us in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.”
— Romans 5:8
While you were still in it.
Jesus didn’t come for perfect people.

He came for proud hearts.
For liars.
For the divided.
For the double-minded.
At the cross, something holy and terrifying happened.

The full weight of what God hates—
sin, rebellion, corruption—

“He Himself bore our sins in His body on the tree…”
— 1 Peter 2:24

Every lie.
Every proud thought.
Every hidden scheme.

You are more sinful than you want to admit—
and more loved than you can imagine.

“If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us… and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.”
— 1 John 1:9
That means the story doesn’t end with:

What are you still holding
that God is calling you to release?

Because delayed obedience
is still disobedience.

Jesus didn’t die
so you could manage sin.

He died
so you could be free from it.
And freedom doesn’t begin with effort.

Right now—yes, right now—
you can pray:

“Jesus, I see it.
I’ve justified what You hate.
Forgive me.
Change me.
I surrender.”

“There is therefore now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus.”
— Romans 8:1
This is God reaching for you.
If this pierced your heart, don’t ignore it.
who needs truth wrapped in grace.
If this stirred something in you…
